prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1448; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the center lane of a multi-lane roadway in Baytown, Texas, when the vehicle moved left to change lanes and made contact with the side of Driver 2's vehicle, which was in the adjacent lane. Driver 1 is the named insured on the policy involved. Responding officers observed scrape marks and paint transfer along the right rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle, consistent with the side-to-side contact described by both drivers, and the damage pattern is in line with the impact reported. Photographs taken at the scene show the vehicle positions and confirm several of the details given by the drivers. No independent witnesses were located, and no prior damage to either vehicle was known to the parties or observed at the scene. Passenger reported neck and upper back pain consistent with whiplash and said the force of the contact threw them against the seat. Passenger's exact seating position in the vehicle could not be fully established during the interview, and the account given on that point was not entirely clear. Passenger was transported for evaluation. Officers did not issue a citation at the scene, and the matter was documented for review.
